analysis.title: Sell Side Indicator: Equity sentiment unchanged, but rotation hits extremes
key_insights: The Sell Side Indicator (SSI), a contrarian signal built from sell side strategists' average recommended equity allocation in a balanced fund, was unchanged at 57.2% in October. That is the highest since March 2022.

The S&P 500 fell about 1% in October, but the move hid extreme rotation. The Russell 1000 Value Index beat Growth by 10ppt, the widest spread since February 2001. The equal-weighted S&P 500 beat the cap-weighted index by 6ppt, the widest since April 2009.
76% of S&P 500 stocks ended October ahead of the cap-weighted index, the highest share in BofA's data history, which starts in 1986.
The SSI is 0.3ppt below the 57.5% Sell threshold and 5.9ppt above the 51.3% Buy threshold, so it sits in Neutral but one step from Sell.

If the SSI enters Sell, median and average next-twelve-month S&P 500 returns have historically been below average but still positive, at 7% and 3%. At this level or higher, NTM returns were negative 36% of the time versus 17% overall since 1985.
Corporate EPS guidance is strong: with 60% of S&P 500 companies having reported 3Q results, the ratio of above- to below-consensus EPS guides was 2.3x last month versus a 1.0x seasonal average.
The market barely differentiated EPS beats from misses (+0.4ppt versus +0.1ppt the next day). Investors focused on cash instead: FCF/EV was the top-performing factor BofA tracks in October (+11%).
40% of BofA FMS investors cite AI capex as the most likely source of a credit event, the top response. A net 7% say payout ratios are too low, the highest in 12+ years.

Historically the SSI has had better predictive power for subsequent 12-month S&P 500 returns (R-squared 25%, 34% at extremes) than other single-factor timing tools such as Proforma PE (8%) and dividend yield (8%).
Average sell side equity allocation remains below the traditional 60-65% balanced-fund band, partly because of rising allocations to alternative investments.

sector_views.rationale: Russell 1000 Value led Growth by 10ppt in October, the widest spread since February 2001. The report describes this as extreme rotation and takes no style call.

earnings_insights: 3Q results from 60% of S&P 500 companies were in as of the report. The ratio of above- to below-consensus EPS guides was 2.3x last month versus a 1.0x seasonal average.
The next-day price reaction to reported EPS beats was +0.4ppt versus +0.1ppt for misses, so the market barely differentiated between them.
risk_factors: The SSI is 0.3ppt from a Sell signal. Historically Sell readings have been followed by the weakest S&P 500 returns (average subsequent 12m +2.7%, 38.9% negative).
AI capex is the top cited source of a potential credit event in the BofA FMS (40% of investors).
Investor focus on cash over EPS suggests strong earnings are not being rewarded.

tension_points.bull_case: EPS guidance is strong, with the ratio of above- to below-consensus guides at 2.3x versus a 1.0x seasonal average. In Sell territory, historical median and average NTM S&P 500 returns were still positive at 7% and 3%.
tension_points.bear_case: The SSI at 57.2% is 0.3ppt from a Sell signal. At this level or higher, NTM returns were negative 36% of the time versus 17% overall. Historically Sell periods saw the weakest 12-month returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move of the SSI above the 57.5% Sell threshold would shift the indicator to a Sell signal.

theme_stances.key_argument: The SSI is 0.3ppt from a Sell signal, and historically such readings carry weaker forward returns.
A 1% S&P 500 decline masked the widest Value-over-Growth spread since 2001 and the widest equal-weight-over-cap-weight spread since 2009.
theme_stances.evidence: masked extreme rotation beneath the surface

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors are rewarding cash generation and payouts over EPS beats, with FCF/EV the top factor in October.
